text: Add a small within-user RankNet term to the experiment 1 pointwise BCE objective so positive impressions are explicitly promoted above negatives for the same user.
rationale: Experiment 1 has strong GAUC but still materially lower nDCG@5, while experiment 3's tab interaction did not improve primary. A ranking-loss change tests objective alignment without expanding feature scope.
exact_ablation: From experiment 1, retain the identical five categorical fields, additive scorer, optimizer, and BCE reduction, and add exactly one auxiliary within-user positive-negative RankNet logistic loss with coefficient 0.10, using only training rows and deterministic same-user pair sampling.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.004 from direct same-user ordering pressure.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.004 if promoted positives cross the top-five boundary.

text: Replace experiment 1 BCE with a bounded same-user RankNet objective to optimize within-user positive-negative ordering directly.
rationale: The official GAUC is within-user AUC, and experiment 1's pointwise objective may leave ordering signal underused. This is materially distinct from adding a small ranking auxiliary term.
exact_ablation: From experiment 1, replace only row-averaged BCE with mean deterministic same-user positive-negative RankNet logistic loss, capped at four sampled negatives per positive; retain features, additive scorer, optimizer, learning rate, and stopping rule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.005 if same-user mixed-label training histories are sufficiently common.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.003 because pairwise ordering may not concentrate enough weight on top-five errors.

text: Add an nDCG@5-swap-weighted pairwise ranking auxiliary to target top-five errors while retaining pointwise BCE stability.
rationale: Large supported tab slices have very poor nDCG@5 despite usable within-user discrimination, indicating that a top-rank-focused objective is more informative than another broad feature interaction.
exact_ablation: From experiment 1, retain all model and data settings and add exactly one LambdaRank-style same-user positive-negative logistic loss weighted by detached absolute nDCG@5 swap change, with coefficient 0.10.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.003 because top-five weighting can trade broad pairwise ordering for head ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.002 to +0.006 by concentrating gradients on positive-negative swaps affecting ranks one through five.

text: Use a mixed BCE-plus-ListNet objective over complete same-user training lists to train direct within-list competition.
rationale: The observed gap between GAUC and nDCG@5 motivates a listwise alternative. This tests list-normalized competition rather than pairwise margin weighting.
exact_ablation: From experiment 1, replace only the training objective with group-mean ListNet top-one cross-entropy on mixed-label same-user training lists plus an item-mean BCE anchor weighted 0.10; retain the five fields, additive scorer, optimizer, and temporal split.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.002 to +0.002 because listwise normalization can weaken broad within-user calibration.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.005 if same-user lists provide meaningful candidate competition.

text: Change early stopping from a GAUC-only proxy to the official primary proxy computed as the mean of GAUC and nDCG@5.
rationale: Experiment 1 was selected by a GAUC-only training proxy although official selection averages GAUC and nDCG@5. This is a cheap alignment correction with no feature or scorer change.
exact_ablation: From experiment 1, change only checkpoint selection and patience monitoring from validation within-user GAUC proxy to validation primary proxy equal to 0.5 times within-user GAUC plus 0.5 times nDCG@5; retain data, features, BCE, optimizer, epoch limit, and patience unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.001 because the selected epoch may sacrifice some broad ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: 0.000 to +0.003 through selection of a more top-five-effective checkpoint.

text: Add a video-by-hour interaction to allow item appeal to vary by time of day.
rationale: Request context was the only positively screened family, and many hour slices have low primary scores. Unlike the failed video-by-tab interaction, this tests temporal context specificity.
exact_ablation: From experiment 1, append exactly one hashed categorical feature for the pair (video_id, hour), fitted by deterministic hashing with a fixed training-independent bucket space; retain all original fields, BCE, scorer, optimizer, and stopping rule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.002 because sparse item-hour cells may not generalize temporally.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: 0.000 to +0.003 if time-specific item appeal improves head ordering.

text: Add a video-by-weekday interaction to model stable day-of-week variation in item appeal.
rationale: Weekday is part of the sole positive train-only context family, while this lower-cardinality interaction should be less sparse than the video-by-tab feature that failed in experiment 3.
exact_ablation: From experiment 1, append exactly one hashed categorical feature for the pair (video_id, weekday), using a fixed hash space and no held-out fitting; retain all original fields, BCE, scorer, optimizer, and stopping rule unchanged.

expected_effect.nDCG@5: 0.000 to +0.003 if weekday effects are stable through validation.

text: Add a tab-by-hour interaction to model time-dependent request-surface effects without expanding item-specific interaction capacity.
rationale: Tab 0 and tab 6 exhibit severe top-five weakness, and request context screened positively. This compact interaction isolates whether time changes surface-level preference patterns.
exact_ablation: From experiment 1, append exactly one categorical feature equal to the pair (tab, hour), with vocabulary fitted on training rows only and an unknown bucket; retain the remaining model, BCE objective, optimizer, and stopping rule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: 0.000 to +0.002 through context-specific score offsets that vary within users.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: 0.000 to +0.003 if the interaction corrects surface-specific head ranking.

text: Add a causal recent-item-repeat indicator that marks whether the candidate video appeared earlier for the user.
rationale: Item IDs work strongly for warm items, while medium-frequency items have very poor nDCG@5. A strictly prior user-item exposure signal tests repeat-consumption behavior without using outcomes or future events.
exact_ablation: From experiment 1, append exactly one binary causal feature indicating whether the same user_id-video_id pair occurred strictly earlier in timestamp order in the standard log, emitting the feature before updating history for each row; retain all other features, BCE, scorer, optimizer, and stopping rule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.000 to +0.003 if repeat exposure is predictive of long-view preference.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.003 because repeated exposures may be fatigue signals rather than preference signals.

text: Add a causal bucketed user history-length feature to condition item scores on the amount of prior exposure.
rationale: Performance varies across user activity segments, including stronger results for middle-active users and weaker full-active users. A causal history-size state is a small test before spending on sequence architecture.
exact_ablation: From experiment 1, append exactly one categorical feature containing a log-bucketed count of strictly earlier standard-log impressions for the user, computed before each row is incorporated into that user's history; retain original fields, BCE, scorer, optimizer, and stopping unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.002 because a user-only term cannot directly reorder a fixed user list unless temporal history differs within that user's rows.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.001 for the same limited within-user-variation reason.

text: Use a compact causal sequence encoder over prior displayed video IDs to provide dynamic user-interest state to the ranker.
rationale: The poor head ranking in supported context slices may reflect missing changing user intent rather than insufficient static interactions. This tests a causal dynamic-interest mechanism that is distinct from all prior experiments.
exact_ablation: From experiment 1, add exactly one causal history representation: a mean-pooled embedding of the last 20 strictly earlier displayed video_ids for each row, concatenated to the existing additive logit through a learned linear projection; retain the existing fields, BCE objective, optimizer, and early-stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.000 to +0.004 if recent displayed-item sequences encode evolving preference.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.005 if candidate ranking benefits from dynamic user state.

text: Reduce additive-model L2 regularization to test whether the validated request-context model is overly shrunk.
rationale: This is a low-cost calibration experiment after two more complex changes underperformed. It adds no features and cleanly distinguishes underfitting from interaction-mechanism failure.
exact_ablation: From experiment 1, change only the L2 coefficient from 1e-6 to 1e-7; retain the identical data, five features, additive scorer, BCE loss, optimizer, learning rate, batching, and stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.001 to +0.001 because lower shrinkage can either preserve useful sparse effects or overfit them.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.002 because head rankings may benefit modestly from less-shrunk context and item weights.
